title: Luke Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Luke 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus healed a man with a withered hand
Disciples plucked ears of corn on the sabbath
Jesus prayed all night on a mountain
questions.correctAnswer: Disciples plucked ears of corn on the sabbath
questions.explanation: The earliest event in the chapter is the disciples plucking ears of corn on the sabbath as recorded in Luke 6:1.

questions.question: What did the disciples do to the ears of corn in Luke 6?
options: They plucked and rubbed them in their hands
They gave them to the Pharisees
questions.correctAnswer: They plucked and rubbed them in their hands
questions.explanation: Luke 6:1 states that the disciples plucked the ears of corn and rubbed them in their hands.

questions.question: Who questioned Jesus' disciples about their actions on the sabbath?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:2 mentions that certain of the Pharisees questioned the disciples about their actions on the sabbath.

questions.question: According to Jesus in Luke 6, who did David eat the shewbread with?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:3-4 state that David ate the shewbread and gave also to those who were with him.

questions.question: What title does Jesus claim for himself in Luke 6?
options: Son of man and Lord of the sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Son of man and Lord of the sabbath
questions.explanation: In Luke 6:5 Jesus states that the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

questions.question: Where did Jesus find the man with the withered right hand?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:6 states that Jesus entered into the synagogue where there was a man whose right hand was withered.

questions.question: Why were the scribes and Pharisees watching Jesus closely in Luke 6?
options: To find an accusation against him if he healed on the sabbath
To invite him to a feast
To ask him questions about the law
questions.correctAnswer: To find an accusation against him if he healed on the sabbath
questions.explanation: Luke 6:7 explains that the scribes and Pharisees watched Jesus to find an accusation if he healed on the sabbath day.

questions.question: What command did Jesus give to the man with the withered hand?
questions.explanation: In Luke 6:10 Jesus commanded the man to stretch forth his hand.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people after Jesus healed the man’s hand?
options: They were filled with madness and plotted against Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: They were filled with madness and plotted against Jesus
questions.explanation: Luke 6:11 says they were filled with madness and communed what they might do to Jesus.

questions.question: How long did Jesus pray on the mountain?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:12 states that Jesus continued all night in prayer on the mountain.

questions.question: How many apostles did Jesus choose in Luke 6?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:13 states that Jesus chose twelve apostles.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus named Simon as Peter among the twelve apostles.
questions.explanation: Luke 6:14 states Simon was also named Peter by Jesus.

questions.question: True or False: Judas Iscariot was called the traitor among the twelve apostles.
questions.explanation: Luke 6:16 identifies Judas Iscariot as the traitor.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Jesus healed a blind man in Luke 6.
questions.explanation: No mention of a blind man being healed is in Luke 6; the healing was of a man with a withered hand (Luke 6:6-10).

questions.question: True or False: The text states that Jesus performed miracles in the region of Galilee in Luke 6.
questions.explanation: Luke 6:17 mentions people coming from Judaea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon but does not mention Galilee.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus declare about those who are poor?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Luke 6:20 says, 'Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.'

questions.question: What does Luke 6:21 promise will happen if someone is hungry now?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Luke 6:21 states, 'Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled.'

questions.question: What should one do to those who hate them, according to Jesus?
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in Luke 6:27, 'But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you.'

questions.question: What does Luke 6:29 suggest when someone strikes you on one cheek?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Luke 6:29 says, 'And unto him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other.'

questions.question: What does Jesus say about the rich in Luke 6:24?
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in Luke 6:24, 'But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.'

questions.question: What does Luke 6:22 say about being hated for the Son of man's sake?
options: It is a cause for mourning
It is a sign of failure
questions.explanation: This is correct because Luke 6:22 mentions, 'Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you... for the Son of man's sake.'

questions.question: What should one do for those who curse them, according to Luke 6:28?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Luke 6:28 instructs, 'Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.'

questions.question: What does Luke 6:31 teach about how we should treat others?
options: Do to others as you would have them do to you
questions.correctAnswer: Do to others as you would have them do to you
questions.explanation: This is correct because Luke 6:31 states, 'And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.'

questions.question: What is the fate of those who laugh now, according to Luke 6:25?
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in Luke 6:25, 'Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.'

questions.question: According to Luke 6:32, what is the significance of loving those who love you?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Luke 6:32 states, 'For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them.'

questions.question: What does Luke 6:33 say about doing good to those who do good to you?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Luke 6:33 highlights that doing good to those who do good to you is what sinners also do.

questions.question: What does Luke 6:34 say about lending to those from whom you expect to receive back?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Luke 6:34 states, 'And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.'

questions.question: Jesus healed those who were vexed with unclean spirits. Is this true?
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in Luke 6:18, 'And they that were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed.'

questions.question: Those who are full will never hunger according to Luke 6:25. Is this true?
questions.explanation: This is false because Luke 6:25 states, 'Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger.'

questions.question: It is considered a blessing to be spoken well of by all men, according to Luke 6:26. Is this true?
questions.explanation: This is false as Luke 6:26 warns, 'Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.'

hard.title: Luke Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 6.

questions.question: What are we instructed to do with our enemies according to Luke 6:35?
questions.explanation: The verse instructs us to love our enemies, which highlights the radical nature of Jesus' teaching on love and forgiveness in Luke 6:35.

questions.question: What will be the reward for lending without expecting anything in return, as stated in Luke 6:35?
options: You will be praised by men
questions.explanation: Luke 6:35 states that your reward will be great if you lend, hoping for nothing in return, emphasizing God's generosity.

questions.question: According to Luke 6:36, how should we behave towards others?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:36 teaches us to be merciful as our Father is merciful, calling for compassion and forgiveness.

questions.question: What principle is illustrated in Luke 6:38 regarding giving?
options: Give and it shall be given unto you
questions.correctAnswer: Give and it shall be given unto you
questions.explanation: Luke 6:38 emphasizes the principle of reciprocity in giving, indicating that generous giving leads to generous receiving.

questions.question: In Luke 6:41, what does Jesus ask about the mote and the beam?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:41 questions why one would notice the mote in their brother's eye while ignoring the beam in their own, teaching self-reflection.

questions.question: What does Luke 6:45 say about what comes out of a person's heart?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:45 states that a good man brings forth good from the treasure of his heart, emphasizing the connection between character and actions.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'agape' in Luke 6:35 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'agape' refers to unconditional love, which is the essence of the command to love one's enemies in Luke 6:35.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Luke 6:37-38?
questions.explanation: In Luke 6:37-38, parallelism is employed to emphasize the reciprocal nature of judgment and mercy, highlighting the balance in divine justice.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of mercy in Luke 6:36?
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:7 states, 'Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy,' echoing the teaching of mercy found in Luke 6:36.

questions.question: Which passage relates to the concept of judgment found in Luke 6:37?
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:1 states, 'Judge not, that ye be not judged,' which parallels the instruction in Luke 6:37 about refraining from judgment.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Luke 6:38?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:37, which discusses judgment and forgiveness, immediately precedes the teaching on giving in Luke 6:38.

questions.question: What is the significance of the metaphor of the tree in Luke 6:43?
questions.explanation: In Luke 6:43, the metaphor of the tree and its fruit signifies that moral character is revealed by one's actions, linking to the theme of integrity.

questions.question: The teaching to love our enemies in Luke 6:35 is consistent with which Old Testament command?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 19:18 states, 'Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself,' which aligns with the teaching in Luke 6:35.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 6:46, Jesus questions why people call Him 'Lord' but do not obey Him.
questions.explanation: Luke 6:46 clearly states that Jesus questions why people call Him 'Lord' and do not do what He says, emphasizing the importance of obedience.

questions.question: True or False: In Luke 6:48, the man who built his house on rock represents those who do not follow Jesus' teachings.
questions.explanation: Luke 6:48 describes the man who built his house on rock as one who hears and does Jesus' sayings, representing the wise follower, not the disobedient.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 6:5 teach about the nature of Jesus in relation to the Sabbath?
options: Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath
Jesus observes the Sabbath law strictly
Jesus is subordinate to the Pharisees regarding the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath
questions.explanation: Luke 6:5 states, 'That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath,' affirming Jesus' divine authority over the Sabbath.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s mercy and human response is taught in Luke 6:36?
options: Believers are called to be merciful as God is merciful
God’s mercy is conditional on human merit
Mercy is reserved only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to be merciful as God is merciful
questions.explanation: Luke 6:36 commands, 'Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful,' teaching the doctrine of imitatio Dei in mercy.

questions.question: What doctrine about the foundation of true discipleship is taught in Luke 6:48?
options: True discipleship is founded on obedience to Jesus’ sayings
Discipleship depends on external religious practices
Faith alone without works is sufficient foundation
Discipleship is based on social status
questions.correctAnswer: True discipleship is founded on obedience to Jesus’ sayings
questions.explanation: Luke 6:48 compares the wise builder who 'doeth' Jesus’ sayings to one who builds on a rock, emphasizing obedience as the foundation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 6:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:8 states Jesus 'knew their thoughts,' demonstrating His attribute of omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Luke 6:35?
questions.explanation: Luke 6:35 says God 'is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil,' highlighting His attribute of kindness.

questions.question: How does Luke 6:12-16 prepare the narrative for the establishment of the twelve apostles and their mission in the New Testament?
options: By showing Jesus’ deliberate choice and prayerful dependence on God in selecting apostles
By emphasizing apostolic authority as inherited from the Pharisees
By focusing on the apostles’ political ambitions
By introducing the apostles as leaders of the Jewish temple
questions.correctAnswer: By showing Jesus’ deliberate choice and prayerful dependence on God in selecting apostles
questions.explanation: Luke 6:12-16 describes Jesus praying all night before choosing twelve apostles, indicating the divine guidance foundational for their mission.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Luke 6:20-23 make by contrasting blessings and woes?
options: It connects the blessings of the kingdom to the experience of Old Testament prophets
It rejects Old Testament promises of prosperity
It teaches that material wealth is the sign of God’s favor
questions.correctAnswer: It connects the blessings of the kingdom to the experience of Old Testament prophets
questions.explanation: Luke 6:23 states that the reward for suffering for Christ is like that of the prophets, linking Jesus’ teaching to redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 6:37 and Luke 6:38 teach about judgment and generosity?
options: Judgment and forgiveness are reciprocal, and generosity will be rewarded in measure
Judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to generosity
Forgiveness is unrelated to human actions
Generosity leads to poverty and judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment and forgiveness are reciprocal, and generosity will be rewarded in measure
questions.explanation: Luke 6:37 teaches not to judge or condemn but to forgive, while 6:38 teaches that giving leads to abundant return, linking mercy and generosity to eternal reward.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about human sin and self-righteousness do Luke 6:41 and Luke 6:42 teach?
options: Hypocrisy blinds self-righteous people from their own sin before correcting others
Judging others is encouraged without self-examination
Sin is only external and not internal
questions.correctAnswer: Hypocrisy blinds self-righteous people from their own sin before correcting others
questions.explanation: Luke 6:41-42 warn against judging others while ignoring one’s greater faults, exposing hypocrisy in human sinfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about the heart and speech do Luke 6:45 and Luke 6:46 teach?
options: The heart’s condition determines speech and obedience to Jesus’ commands
Speech is unrelated to the heart’s condition
Obedience to Jesus is not necessary for discipleship
The heart is unknowable and irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: The heart’s condition determines speech and obedience to Jesus’ commands
questions.explanation: Luke 6:45 relates speech to the heart’s treasure; 6:46 challenges calling Jesus Lord without doing His words, linking heart, speech, and obedience.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jesus’ teaching in Luke 6:27-36 promotes passivity toward evil. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches active love and mercy toward enemies, not passivity or enabling evil
It allows hatred as justified response
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches active love and mercy toward enemies, not passivity or enabling evil
questions.explanation: Luke 6:27-36 commands love, blessing, and mercy toward enemies, emphasizing active goodness and kindness despite opposition.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of true blessing and woe is taught in Luke 6:24-26?
options: True blessing is often reversed from worldly status, showing God’s sovereign judgment
Blessings and woes are purely economic
Woe is unrelated to spiritual condition
Blessings are given according to human merit
questions.correctAnswer: True blessing is often reversed from worldly status, showing God’s sovereign judgment
questions.explanation: Luke 6:24-26 pronounces woes on the rich and full, blessings on the poor and hungry, illustrating God’s reversal of worldly values.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Jesus’ healing on the Sabbath in Luke 6:9-10?
questions.explanation: Jesus heals the man’s withered hand on the Sabbath (Luke 6:9-10) to do good rather than evil, showing God’s attribute of mercy over legalism.

questions.question: What theological principle about leadership and discipleship is taught in Luke 6:40?
options: A disciple’s maturity allows him to become like his master
Disciples are always superior to their masters
questions.correctAnswer: A disciple’s maturity allows him to become like his master
questions.explanation: Luke 6:40 teaches that a disciple who is perfect will be like his master, emphasizing the goal of discipleship to conform to Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of true discipleship and divine judgment is taught in Luke 6:47-49?
options: Obedience to Jesus’ words is the foundation that withstands judgment
Judgment is random and not related to obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to Jesus’ words is the foundation that withstands judgment
questions.explanation: Luke 6:47-49 contrasts those who hear and do Jesus’ sayings with those who do not, teaching obedience as the foundation for enduring judgment.
